Subject: Novamarx: post-demo alignment & open questions

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick written recap so we have the same list of pain points, goals, and immediate asks before we schedule a technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what you shared (pain points)
- Current inference latency spikes: P95 ~250–320ms for the reranker path under realistic load; P50 much lower.
- Periodic throughput bursts during batch scoring windows (up to ~180 QPS sustained for 5–10 minutes).
- Sensitive customer data in prompt context -> on-prem/VPC requirement and strict audit logging.
- Costs are ballooning on your current setup when you scale to 100k users.

Goals you outlined
- Target production SLO: P95 <= 120ms for the 1–2k token ranking flow, and P50 <= 45ms for the fast path.
- Support mixed workloads: synchronous single-turn re-ranker + async bulk rerank jobs.
- Maintain auditability (request/response idempotence, retained logs for 13 months).

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed on
1) Technical deep-dive to validate topology and SLO feasibility (include infra, security, and your ML engineer).  
2) Baseline benchmarking run with a small dataset and representative prompts.
3) Draft mutual action plan (timeline + milestones + procurement ask).

Proposed logistics
- Proposed deep-dive slot: Tue/Mar 7 or Wed/Mar 8, 09:00–11:00 PT. Can you confirm availability?

Stuff we'll bring to the deep-dive
- Proposed topology sketch for a Dedicated deployment with burst capacity, prefix/KV caching, and autoscale policies.
- Cost/throughput tradeoffs for quantized variants.
- SOC2 / compliance checklist and standard on-prem packaging notes.

Attachments: I'll follow up with a short technical sketch and SLO worksheet (turnaround within 24 hours).

Thanks — Jasmine

--

Thanks Jasmine — solid recap, appreciate the crisp bullets. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 250–320ms numbers are what we see end-to-end today (our infra + model). The product team is comfortable targeting 120ms P95 but wants to understand the tradeoffs (accuracy vs latency) for quantized models.
- Throughput bursts are driven by our nightly scoring window but they also spike when imports finish; we can provide a replay of traffic shape.
- Security: SOC2 Type II and an internal security questionnaire are gating items for procurement right now.

Availability: Tue/Mar 7 09:00 PT works for our infra lead (Samir) and me. Procurement will join if we get an initial cost estimate.

One more ask: can you include a short section on how Redwood handles model rollbacks and automatic fallback policies when a newer model shows regression? That was a key point for our ML lead.

Alex — thanks, noted. Attached are the short topology sketch and an SLO worksheet that maps your traffic shapes to capacity sizing. High-level highlights below; see attachments for the numbers and the runbook draft.

Attachment stubs:
- novamarx-deep-dive-topology.pdf (PDF, 3p) — topology sketches and runbook snippets
- novamarx-slo-proposal.csv (CSV) — throughput/latency sizing and cost estimate rows
- redwood-mop-stub.txt (TXT) — mutual action plan outline

Technical deep-dive highlights (summary)
- Proposed deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) in us-west-2 with a small Hybrid-VPC control plane for audit logs.  
- Routing: smart routing policy that favors low-latency hosts (pinned pool) for the fast path, with a fallback pool for cost-sensitive batched jobs.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes; use a 48GB KV cache per node to keep top-K states hot. This reduces cold-start P95 markedly.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching with dynamic windowing. For the reranker (1–2k tokens), target batch size 8–16 for best latency/cost balance; for nightly bulk jobs use batch size 64–128 offline.
- Quantization: 4-bit (qlora/ptq) variants recommended for bulk scoring; keep a 16-bit or 8-bit variant pinned for the fast path to guarantee accuracy on production queries where slippage is sensitive.

SLO & capacity examples (see CSV for full rows)
- Fast path (synchronous reranker): target P95 <= 120ms. Estimate: with pinned pool of 4x A100-80GB-equivalent instances, we cover ~150 QPS steady-state with KV hot-hit rates >= 85%.
- Bulk scoring window: autoscale to add 6 nodes for short bursts (5–15 minutes) to handle 180 QPS with batch size 64; use burst credits from Dedicated burst pool to avoid cold provisioning.

Fallback & rollbacks (brief)
- Canary rollouts by sampling 5–10% traffic; automatic regression monitors (latency, token delta, and a sample prompt set) trigger instant rollback to the previous pinned variant. We keep last-3 versions and can do fast pinning to a safe model.

Security & compliance notes
- SOC2 artifacts: we provide standard reports and an evidence pack; for on-prem we offer a packaged bundle with KMS integration and audit log forwarding to your SIEM.

Next action items (short)
1) Confirm Tue/Mar 7 09:00 PT for the deep-dive (Samir, Alex, procurement if available).
2) We run a 2-hour baseline benchmark the week of Mar 13 (you provide traffic replay + small sample dataset).
3) Procurement POV: we'll produce a preliminary cost bake before the benchmarking run so procurement has an estimate.

If that reads okay I'll schedule the deep-dive and invite our infra engineer (Markus) + solutions engineer (Laura) and include the runbook in calendar invite.

Thanks, Jasmine

--
